CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of human trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.
16. Return is an effort to return victims of human trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; return; social reintegration, and legal aid.
21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as return and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and code of conduct for the social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

CHAPTER IV
AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITY
Article 5
(1) The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
 a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;
 b. monitoring and strengthening/support for victims of violence;
 c. capacity building of officials and other stakeholders.

Article 3
The objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. to protect women and children victims of violence;
b. to provide services to women and children victims of acts of violence; and
c. empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 13
(1) Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
The principles of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; and
c. legal certainty.

Article 14
(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related SKPD on a regular basis.
(2) Monitoring is conducted from the planning stage up to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TABANAN REGENCY
NUMBER 11 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

CHAPTER XII
FUNDING
Article 20
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful sources.

REGENT OF TABANAN
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

Article 15
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

REGENT OF TABANAN
PROVINCE OF BALI
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TABANAN REGENCY
NUMBER 11 YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

CHAPTER IX
REPORTING
Article 16
(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence and submitting it to the Governor, with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
(2) Reporting on implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

Article 18
The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the region.

Article 16
Sufficiently clear

Article 20
Sufficiently clear

CHAPTER VII
SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSE
Article 12
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or a Safe House or other designation.
(2) The Social Protection House and/or Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) guarantees, in the implementation of services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.
(3) For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), regional governments may make use of social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

REGENT OF TABANAN,
NI PUTU EKA WIRYASTUTI
Promulgated in Tabanan on September 9, 2016

Sufficiently clear.

ELUCIDATION

NUMBER 11 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

REGENT OF TABANAN
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

CHAPTER XII
FUNDING
Article 20
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful sources.

CHAPTER IX
REPORTING
Article 16
(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence and submitting it to the Governor, with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
(2) Reporting on implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IX
REPORTING

(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER IV
AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITY
Article 5

 b. monitoring and strengthening/support for victims of violence;
 c. capacity building of officials and other stakeholders.

Article 12
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or a Safe House or other designation.

(3) For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), regional governments may make use of social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of human trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.
16. Return is an effort to return victims of human trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; return; social reintegration, and legal aid.
21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as return and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and code of conduct for the social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 18
The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the region.

Article 8
Letter a What is meant by adequate supporting facilities and infrastructure is adjusted to the minimum service standards and standard operating procedures for repatriation and social reintegration that apply.
Letter b What is meant by implementing officers or functional officers includes health workers, psychologists, psychiatrists, social workers provided by relevant agencies or institutions.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.

Sufficiently clear

a. adequate supporting facilities and infrastructure; b. implementing officers; and

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
The principles of implementing protection for women and children victims of violence are:
a. justice and gender equality;
b. non-discrimination; and
c. legal certainty.

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of human trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.
16. Return is an effort to return victims of human trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; return; social reintegration, and legal aid.
21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as return and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and code of conduct for the social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

NUMBER 11 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of human trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.
16. Return is an effort to return victims of human trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; return; social reintegration, and legal aid.
21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as return and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and code of conduct for the social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

FUNDING
Article 20
The implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
b. other lawful sources.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TABANAN REGENCY
NUMBER 11 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

Article 14
(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related SKPD on a regular basis.
(2) Monitoring is conducted from the planning stage up to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

Article 15
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 13
(1) Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1

7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. 12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.

16. Return is an effort to return victims of human trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. 24. SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSE

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

NUMBER 11 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights. As is known, the human rights of women and children have been guaranteed and regulated in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia and the Law on Human Rights. Therefore, the protection of the rights of women and children from violence should be respected, enforced, and human dignity enhanced without discrimination, so as to realize welfare and justice for women and children.
Violence is any unlawful act, with or without the use of means, directed at the physical and psychological, that causes danger to life or the body, or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against children is any act against children that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of children. The existence of women and children victims of violence has not yet received adequate services so that minimum services for victims of violence are needed.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Tabanan Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for women and children victims of violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in Tabanan Regency.

CHAPTER VII
SOCIAL PROTECTION HOUSE
Article 12
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to establish a Social Protection House and/or a Safe House or other designation.
(2) The Social Protection House and/or Safe House as referred to in paragraph (1) guarantees, in the implementation of services, health rehabilitation, social rehabilitation, repatriation, and social reintegration.
(3) For the provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2), regional governments may make use of social protection houses and/or Safe Houses owned by the community or other social service institutions.

CHAPTER IV
AUTHORITY AND RESPONSIBILITY
Article 5
(1) The Regional Government has the authority and responsibility for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
 a. service activities for women and children victims of violence;
 b. monitoring and strengthening/support for victims of violence;
 c. capacity building of officials and other stakeholders.

Article 14
(1) Monitoring is conducted through coordination and direct monitoring of related SKPD on a regular basis.
(2) Monitoring is conducted from the planning stage up to the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence for the current year.

CHAPTER VIII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 13
(1) Regional Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children victims of violence in the region.

CHAPTER IX
REPORTING
Article 16
(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing a report on the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence and submitting it to the Governor, with a copy submitted to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.
(2) Reporting on implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually.
(3) Further provisions regarding the procedures and form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Tabanan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tabanan.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Tabanan Regency.
5. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
6. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including an unborn child.
8. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
9. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child committed by parties who should be responsible for the child or those who have power over the child.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
12. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
13. Complaint service is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community.
14. Health rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of human trafficking from health disorders they suffer.
15. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions properly.
16. Return is an effort to return victims of human trafficking from the regency area to their area of origin.
17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
18. Legal Aid is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power of attorney, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including complaint services, health rehabilitation; social rehabilitation; return; social reintegration, and legal aid.
21. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as return and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
22. Desa Pakraman is a customary law community unit in Bali Province that has a unified tradition and code of conduct for the social life of the Hindu community passed down through generations in the bond of kahyangan tiga or kahyangan desa which has a certain territory and its own assets and has the right to manage its own household.
23. Social Protection House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
24. Village is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin and/or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia.

Article 18
The Regent conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of SPM for Integrated Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the region.
